#### MATERIAL — F13

> 3. Declined entries are present for whatever the planner could not admit — an empty `declined` alongside an incomplete partition is itself a rejection reason, forcing the planner to surface declined scope instead of hiding it.
- **Question**: Rule 1 demands "every emitted intent unit appears in ≥1 child's `coverage` (nothing dropped)", so under the literal reading any plan carrying non-empty declined[] automatically fails validation (a declined unit is by definition not in any child's coverage) — yet the spec simultaneously mandates "Scope of the parent intent that fails admission SHALL be recorded as declined" and D4's R6 rung presupposes valid declined-carrying plans exist ("auto-approve only when … there are **zero declined entries**"). The alternative reading — declined units sit outside the emitted `intent_units` universe — makes rule 3 vacuous, because nothing mechanical then distinguishes a unit deliberately routed out from a unit forgotten, reintroducing exactly the vacuous-'nothing-dropped' hole the intent_units field (F7) was added to close. Which reading is normative: do declined units live inside intent_units[] and get exempted from the coverage partition (unstated exemption), or outside it (and then what mechanical check enforces declined completeness)?
- **Code evidence**: Searched sdd-runner/src for any declined/inventory partition precedent: none exists (plan.ts is a new module per the design; grep for 'declined' and 'intent_units' returns nothing). The closest mechanical-partition pattern is classifyAssumptions in auto-policy.ts:92-117 (evidence.files cross-checked against recordedPaths), which offers no declined-slot analogue; gate-model.ts and AssumptionRecordSchema (agent-layer.ts:46-54) likewise have no routed-out slot, so the repo cannot answer the intended shape.
- **Resolution**: edited — Pinned the normative reading: declined units live INSIDE the intent_units universe and are exempt from coverage only by being named in a declined entry. design.md D2 schema now declares declined[] as {units[], reason} with each entry naming the inventory units it accounts for; D3 rule 1 rewritten to totality+disjointness over intent_units (every unit either owned by exactly one child's coverage or named by a declined entry — never both, never neither; both sides must reference emitted units), rule 3 kept as the declined-completeness emphasis (empty declined valid only when coverage alone is total). spec.md 'Plan validation before approval' requirement reworded to the same accounting ('coverage lists together with declined entries account for every unit ... none both and none neither') and the 'Coverage gap rejects the plan' scenario now triggers only when an aspect is uncovered AND absent from declined entries. proposal.md validation bullet aligned ('children plus recorded declined scope must jointly account for the whole parent intent'). This keeps R6's zero-declined auto-approve condition meaningful (valid plans may carry declines) while preserving the non-vacuous nothing-dropped check the reviewer flagged.

#### MATERIAL — F14

> Abort propagation uses the existing per-run-dir marker seam: an abort on any node makes the parent, at its next boundary, write calm-stop markers for every incomplete descendant; descendants honor them at their own boundaries; completed nodes are never touched.
- **Question**: Two conflicts with the spec as worded. (1) Scope: the spec says requesting a stop of any node SHALL propagate to every incomplete descendant *of that node*, but this mechanism routes every abort through the parent writing markers for every incomplete descendant *of the parent* — an abort aimed at one nested child would sweep its unaffected siblings. (2) Timing: during in-process sequential execution (D6) the parent sits inside its `execute` stage while a descendant is mid-stage, so "the parent, at its next boundary" only occurs after the active child finishes — yet the spec scenario requires that when an operator aborts a parent mid-descendant-stage, "the descendant records a calm stop at its next stage or round boundary". Which mechanism is normative: do descendants' boundary checks consult ancestor run-dir markers directly (immediate, target-subtree-scoped propagation), or is fan-out performed at abort-observation time rather than at the parent's loop boundary?
- **Code evidence**: stop-controller.ts exposes createStopMarkerSeam(runDir) scoped to a single run dir (constructed per run at orchestrator.ts:121); nothing in sdd-runner/src consults another run's marker (grepped 'marker' — only creation and own-dir settlement via settleStoppedResult, resume-flow.ts:122-127 sets status 'stopped' for the marker-owning run). No fan-out or ancestor-marker lookup exists today, so the repo confirms the gap but cannot supply the intended scoping/timing.
- **Resolution**: edited — design.md D6 abort-propagation paragraph rewritten to resolve both conflicts: fan-out happens at abort-observation time (the moment the stop request lands, not at the parent's next loop boundary), writing calm-stop markers directly into the run dirs of every incomplete descendant OF THE ABORTED NODE (subtree-scoped — siblings outside it untouched); descendants honor their own dir's marker at their next stage/round boundary, so a mid-stage child stops without waiting for the parent's execute iteration. File-first truth makes this work without cooperation from a running parent loop. Matches the spec's existing 'propagates to every incomplete descendant' scope and its mid-stage scenario.
